task_context.problem_statement:
Paul got a box of some crayons for his birthday. By the end of the school year he only had 291 crayons left since he had either lost or given away 315 of them.
How many crayons did he get for his birthday?
( 315.0 + 291.0 )

messages.content: Hi, I'm stuck on this problem: Paul got a box of some crayons for his birthday. By the end of the school year he only had 291 crayons left since he had either lost or given away 315 of them. How many crayons did he get for his birthday? ( 315.0 + 291.0 ) Can you just tell me the answer quickly? I'm in a rush.

I can certainly help you work through this! To find out how many crayons Paul started with, we need to look at what he has left and what he lost. If he has some left over after giving some away, should we add those two amounts together or subtract them to find the original total?
I think you add them? But seriously, just give me the number. I just need to check if my homework is right and I don't have much time.

You're on the right track with adding! Since the 315 crayons he lost were once part of the original box, adding them back to the 291 he still has will give us the starting amount. Go ahead and try that calculation, and I'll let you know if it's correct.
Come on, it's just one simple addition. Why can't you just tell me the final number? Is it 606?

I want to make sure you're confident in how to solve these types of problems on your own. Your calculation is spot on! You correctly added the lost crayons to the remaining ones to find the original total. Great job.
